ENGLISH MARCH — GENERAL ASSESSMENT #7
====

GRADE: Grade 12
SUBJECT: ENGLISH MARCH
TIME ALLOWED: 45 minutes
TOTAL MARKS: 30
EXAM BODY: KNEC / KCSE pathway

INSTRUCTIONS
----
1. Answer all questions.
2. For calculations, show formula → substitution → steps → final answer with units.
3. For multiple choice, choose the best option.
4. Check your work before submitting.

SECTION A — MULTIPLE CHOICE
----
1. A noun is a word that names: (1 mark)
   A. Only a joining word
   B. Only a describing word
   C. A person, place, thing, or idea
   D. Only an action

2. When practising Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 2.2.1 Extensive Reading.

3. When practising Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   C. Use insults to “practise” Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Reading 1.2.1 Reading Fluency: Argumentative texts.

4. When practising Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Avoid reading anything related to Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   B. Use insults to “practise” Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .
   D. Copy random text without understanding Writing 1.4.1 Sentence skills: Sentence fluency ● avoiding ambiguity in pronoun .

5. The past tense of “go” is: (1 mark)
   A. going
   B. goed
   C. went
   D. goes

6. Which word is a verb? (1 mark)
   A. quickly
   B. blue
   C. happiness
   D. run

7. When practising Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes ● formation of nouns (nouns formed from other , which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes ● formation of nouns (nouns formed from other .
   B. Use insults to “practise” Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes ● formation of nouns (nouns formed from other .
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes ● formation of nouns (nouns formed from other .
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Grammar in Use 1.3.1 Word classes ● formation of nouns (nouns formed from other .

8. When practising Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   C. Copy random text without understanding Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.
   D. Avoid reading anything related to Critical Listening ● finding connections between ideas or incidents , cause-effe.

9. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   B. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   C. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.
   D. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.2 Conversational Skills: Sounds and discourse markers.

10. When practising Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id, which approach is best? (1 mark)
   A. Use insults to “practise” Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   B. Avoid reading anything related to Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   C. Use clear examples, correct form, and a short local context for Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.
   D. Copy random text without understanding Listening and Speaking 2.1.1 Critical Listening ● finding connections between id.

11. A paragraph should usually have: (1 mark)
   A. Many unrelated topics with no link
   B. One main idea with supporting sentences
   C. No full stops
   D. Only one word repeated

12. Choose the correctly punctuated sentence. (1 mark)
   A. Where is the library?
   B. Where is the library
   C. where is the library
   D. Where is the Library

SECTION B — STRUCTURED / SHORT ANSWERS
----
13. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking ● Responsive Listening: Interpretive listening and making and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

14. In three clear sentences, explain Listening and Speaking 6.1.2 Sounds and stress ● sounds: double consonant cluste and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

15. In three clear sentences, explain Reading 6.2.1 Reading: Fluency: Grade appropriate text (poem, narrative or extra and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)

16. In three clear sentences, explain Grammar in Use 6.3.1 Clauses ● relative clauses: defining and non-defining ● adv and give one Kenyan example. (4 marks)
